messages:
kevin: thinking about a simpler model for graceful eviction + weight-based routing by plan/region. want opinions before I sketch UI.
maya: curious — is this about preempting requests when capacity is tight, or just routing preference? short expl?
kevin: both. goal: when GPU pools hit pressure, we demote traffic from free -> pro -> enterprise in that order, but not binary deny. instead reduce weight and use variant fallbacks.
ashwin: +1 on soft degradation. needs concrete knobs: weight, grace_window, min_qps_per_tenant.
olivia: also need an audit trail in the console and telemetry so customers can see when they were demoted and why.
kevin: sketch of policy I had in mind:
```
{
  "tiers": [
    {"name": "free", "weight": 0.2, "eviction_priority": 100, "grace_window_secs": 30},
    {"name": "pro",  "weight": 0.6, "eviction_priority": 50,  "grace_window_secs": 20},
    {"name": "enterprise","weight": 1.0,"eviction_priority": 0,   "grace_window_secs": 5}
  ],
  "region_overrides": {"eu": {"free": {"weight": 0.15}}},
  "fallback_variants": ["quantized-8bit","smaller-ctx"]
}
```
maya: so weight is relative routing share, and eviction_priority is ordering for hard cut? sounds reasonable.
kevin: exactly. eviction_priority only used for hard cut (if system goes into deny mode). otherwise we scale weights down by pressure factor.
ashwin: impl note: runtime needs to expose current effective weight in /internal route decision API so telemetry can show "expected qps" vs "served qps".
olivia: UI: show a per-tenant timeline with dots for "weight change" events and an expandable detail listing fallback variant used. also surface "reason: region pressure" etc.
ops-bot: alert: pool gpu-eu-03 above 85% for 3m. suggested action: apply weight-shed step 1.
kevin: ops-bot, can we include suggested step in alert payload? like recommended weights per tier? ops-bot: yes.
maya: debate: should weights be absolute per-tenant or relative across tenants in same plan? i prefer relative per-tenant so small free tenants don't get 0.
ashwin: agree, relative per-tenant with min_weight floor. add min_weight config.
kevin: updated policy idea snippet:
```
{"tiers":[{"name":"free","min_weight":0.05}], "global_pressure_factor": 0.7}
```
olivia: telemetry: add metrics: routing.effective_weight{tier,region}, routing.fallback_used{variant}, routing.denied_requests{tier}. hook these into per-route dashboard.
kevin: rollout plan: feature-flag the new policy editor and runtime opt-in. start with internal tenants + 5 beta customers. collect metrics for 48h before enabling auto-shed.
maya: UX: editor should offer presets (conservative/aggressive) and a preview simulator that lets you feed current load and see simulated demotion timeline.
ashwin: API change: add /v1/policies/preview that returns per-tenant effective weights given current infra signals. no change to request path.
kevin: last q: enforcement — do we let routing return 429 for denied traffic or always fallback variant? my vote: prefer fallback variant then 429 as last resort.
olivia: +1. also add a tenant-facing notification webhook when tenant is served a fallback variant for >5m.
kevin: sounds good. I'll prototype the editor JSON -> runtime translation and post a short PR with tests.
olivia: thanks. also, can we add an audit log entry whenever a policy is changed? compliance wants that.
kevin: yes, policy changes will emit audit events and console timeline entries. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag routing-weighting v1 -> canary group at 1990012355 by kevin."
